old: In formal academic discourse, speculative hypotheses are introduced using complex conditional conjunctions. The compound phrase 'feltéve, ha...' (provided that / assuming that) sets up a strict preliminary premise under which a theoretical model or physical prediction holds true: 'A modell érvényes, feltéve, ha az elektronok energiája nem haladja meg a határértéket.'
new: You know *amennyiben* ('if', formal) from B2 Unit 13 and *azzal a feltétellel, hogy* ('on condition that') from B1 Unit 67; B2 Unit 69 used both for hypotheses about technology. In science writing they name the condition under which a model or a prediction holds true: 'A modell érvényes, amennyiben az elektronok energiája nem haladja meg a határértéket.'
why: C1 form feltéve, ha replaced by the known amennyiben; recap with the units from the knowledge sheet (this unit replays Unit 69).

old: The laser pulses can be accurately measured, provided that the detectors' sensitivity reaches the desired level.

old: In high-register administrative, technical, and scientific prose, 'amennyiben' replaces everyday 'ha'. It signals an objective, institutional contingency: 'Amennyiben a pályázat megfelel a követelményeknek, a bizottság mérési időt biztosít az ELI laboratóriumában.'
new: You know *amennyiben* and *abban az esetben, ha* from B2 Unit 13. In administrative, technical and scientific prose they replace everyday *ha* and name an objective, institutional condition: 'Amennyiben a pályázat megfelel a követelményeknek, a bizottság mérési időt biztosít az ELI laboratóriumában.'
why: Recap of the known forms; unit named from the knowledge sheet.

old: 'Hacsak nem...' (unless / except if) introduces the sole mitigating circumstance that can reverse an otherwise inevitable outcome. It is followed by an indicative or conditional verb depending on whether the exception is factual or hypothetical: 'A beruházás sikeres lesz, hacsak nem lépnek fel váratlan hálózati zavarok.'
new: To say 'if not', put *nem* before the verb inside the *amennyiben* clause: 'A beruházás sikeres lesz, amennyiben nem lépnek fel váratlan hálózati zavarok.'
why: hacsak nem replaced by amennyiben ... nem.

old: The experiment will be concluded tomorrow morning, unless they experience unexpected vibrations in the foundation.
new: The experiment will be finished tomorrow morning if they do not notice unexpected vibrations in the foundation.
why: English follows the replaced example.

old: Provided that sufficient international researchers arrive, the facility's capacity will be further expanded.
new: If enough international researchers arrive, the facility's capacity will be expanded further.
why: 'Provided that' invites the C1 *feltéve* reading; plain English for amennyiben.

old: Avoid double negatives: 'hacsak nem' already contains negation, so the verb that follows must not take a redundant 'nem': write 'hacsak nem történik hiba' (unless an error happens), never 'hacsak nem nem történik hiba'.
new: In an *amennyiben* clause the negative word *nem* stands directly before the verb: 'amennyiben nem történik hiba' (if no error happens).
why: Tip belonged to hacsak nem.

old: Foresight analysis synthesizes multiple conditional layers to weigh alternative scenarios. By combining 'feltéve, ha...', 'amennyiben...', 'hacsak nem...', and counterfactual reflections, an author evaluates complex probabilistic futures without asserting dogmatic certainty.
